instructions: Put 1 1/2 cups of the basmati rice in a fine strainer and rinse it under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and a pinch of salt.
Bring the rice to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, mince the garlic and grate the ginger. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Heat the coconut oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds. After about 20 seconds they'll sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the onion and a big pinch of salt. Cook for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and golden at the edges.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute, until you can smell them. Don't let the garlic brown.
Add the curry powder and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the crushed tomatoes and 1 tsp salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes darken and thicken.

Shake the can of coconut milk, then pour it in along with the chickpeas. Bring it to a gentle bubble and cook uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Press a few of the chickpeas against the side of the pan with your spoon to thicken the sauce.
Add the spinach a handful at a time and stir for about 2 minutes, until it wilts. Take the pan off the heat.
Stir in the garam masala, the juice of the lime and 1/4 cup of chopped cilantro.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lime.
method_notes: The sources agree on an onion, garlic and ginger base, curry powder or garam masala, tomato, canned chickpeas and coconut milk, with lime at the end. They differ on spinach (one stirs it in, the others leave it out) and on how much simmering the coconut gets, from 10 to 15 minutes. This version follows the lead's order and adds the spinach and a cumin seed bloom for texture and depth. It is vegan and gluten-free as written: coconut oil instead of ghee, and plain spices with no wheat-based fillers.
